markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if Seasonal Opening Operations occur before the specified date or if the Source Agency reports that the ski resort will not open during the season.
markets.rules_primary: If the first calendar day in the 26/27 winter season on which Sugarbush conducts Seasonal Opening Operations is before Nov 15, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on resort-designated open terrain. 
The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time.
A name, owner, operator, or website change does not change the resort's identity.
If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria
Season-passholder-only access counts if it requires no additional purchase. 
Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count.
If its terrain is split across separately operated areas, opening any portion counts. 

Doesn't count for payout
Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count.
Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count.
Announced or projected dates do not count. 

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with Sugarbush or Alterra Mountain Company. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.rules_primary: If a bill capping federal student loan interest rates has passed the House after Issuance and before Oct 2, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A qualifying bill is legislation that would set, for at least one category of federal student loan, a maximum interest rate lower than the maximum applicable to that category under the law in force on the Issuance date. A rate of zero qualifies. Legislation that re-enacts or technically amends the existing maximums without lowering any of them does NOT qualify, and neither does a cap on fees, monthly payments or total repayment.

The measure must pass the full House by any means, including voice vote, unanimous consent, suspension of the rules, a special rule or a discharge petition. It may be any vehicle, including a larger package whose text as passed contains a qualifying cap. Committee approval, a rule providing for consideration, or a discharge petition reaching 218 signatures without passage does NOT count. Senate passage, enactment, and a cap imposed by regulation rather than by the House do NOT count.

markets.rules_secondary:
Losing a committee assignment refers to Haley Stevens ceasing to be a member of any House committee or subcommittee she sits on, or ceasing to be the ranking member of the Research and Technology Subcommittee, for any reason. This includes removal by the House, the House Democratic Caucus or party leadership, leaving the House Democratic Caucus, stepping down from the position, or leaving the House. The end of her House term on Jan 3, 2027 does NOT count.

Only reporting from the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives or any other Source Agency qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

markets.rules_secondary:
If Haley Stevens changes their official party registration from the Democratic Party to another party or to independent/unaffiliated status, announces they are no longer a member of the House Democratic Caucus, or is expelled from the House Democratic Caucus by official party action, then the market will resolve to Yes.

Announcing a switch to another party or to independent status, or joining the House Republican Conference, counts as leaving the House Democratic Caucus.

The following do NOT count:
Being stripped of committee assignments while remaining in the House Democratic Caucus.
Temporary suspension from caucus activities or committees while remaining a member.
Loss of party endorsement or support while remaining a member.
Statements about considering leaving without actual departure.
Resignation from Congress or expulsion from Congress.

markets.rules_primary: If the first calendar day in the 2026-27 winter season on which Snowbird Ski Resort conducts Seasonal Opening Operations occurs before Nov 22, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on terrain designated open for that use by Snowbird Ski Resort.
The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time.
The season runs from September 1 through August 31 of the following year. “Before” excludes the specified date.
A name, branding, ownership, operator, or website change does not change the resort’s geographic identity.
If Snowbird Ski Resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria
Access counts only when holders of a season pass valid for the specified season can use those lifts and terrain without an additional purchase.
Free reservations and passholder-only days count. 
Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count.

Doesn’t count for payout
Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count.
Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count.
Scheduled, projected, or announced opening dates do not count.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Snowbird Ski Resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

The qualifying vote is the House's first vote on adopting a resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth, whether or not it is adopted. If the House votes on that resolution's articles separately, voting for any of its articles counts as voting for the resolution.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if Seasonal Opening Operations occur before the specified date or if the Source Agency reports that the ski resort will not open during the season.
markets.rules_primary: If the first calendar day in the 26/27 winter season on which Deer Valley conducts Seasonal Opening Operations is before Nov 22, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on resort-designated open terrain. 
The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time.
A name, owner, operator, or website change does not change the resort's identity.
If the ski resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria
Season-passholder-only access counts if it requires no additional purchase. 
Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count.
If its terrain is split across separately operated areas, opening any portion counts. 

Doesn't count for payout
Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count.
Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count.
Announced or projected dates do not count. 

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with Deer Valley or Alterra Mountain Company. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the endorsement occurs or once the Senate Democratic Caucus has elected its leader for the 120th Congress.
markets.rules_primary: If Scott Colom publicly endorses Chuck Schumer in the Senate Democratic leadership election for the 120th Congress before Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
To back Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, Scott Colom must make an "endorsement", which requires:
A clear, affirmative statement of support for Chuck Schumer's election as Senate Democratic leader, or that Scott Colom will vote for Chuck Schumer for that post
The statement must be public (not private communications)
The statement must specifically reference the Senate Democratic leadership election for the 120th Congress or be clearly in context of it
The statement must come directly from Scott Colom or through official channels

The following scenarios would resolve to YES:
Scott Colom states "I endorse Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader"
Scott Colom states "I support Chuck Schumer" with clear reference to the Senate Democratic leadership election
Scott Colom states "I'm voting for Chuck Schumer" publicly
Scott Colom states "Chuck Schumer has my full support" for Senate Democratic leader
Scott Colom releases official endorsement through his office or campaign

Statements of obvious sarcasm (or which are immediately followed by clarifications that Scott Colom is joking) are NOT encompassed by the Payout Criterion.

The Contract shall resolve immediately upon confirmation of the first qualifying endorsement by Scott Colom in the specified race. A statement made after the Senate Democratic Caucus has elected its leader for the 120th Congress does not qualify. If no qualifying endorsement of Chuck Schumer occurs before that election or before Jan 3, 2027, whichever is first, this market resolves to No.

If Chuck Schumer withdraws from or ceases to be a candidate in the specified race before a qualifying endorsement is confirmed, this market may resolve to No in the sole discretion of the Exchange.

An endorsement conditioned only on Chuck Schumer declaring candidacy for, filing for, entering, or remaining in this race qualifies when the statement is confirmed. An endorsement subject to any other condition does not qualify. On social media, only verified accounts qualify; likes or retweets alone do not count. A quote tweet with added commentary must meet the endorsement requirements above.
markets.title: Will Scott Colom endorse Chuck Schumer in the Senate Democratic leadership election for the 120th Congress before Jan 3, 2027?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if all elections have been decided and margins calculated.
markets.rules_primary: If Minnesota has the smallest margin of victory among all elections in the 2026 United States Senate elections as of Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Margin of victory is calculated as the absolute percentage point difference between first and second place finishers. For two-candidate races, this is winner's percentage minus runner-up's percentage. For multi-candidate races, only the gap between first and second counts. For ranked choice/instant runoff elections, the margin from the final round is used. If no candidate wins a majority in Georgia and a runoff is held, the margin from the December 1, 2026 runoff is used.

If official results aren't available by the deadline but at least 95% of expected vote is counted, preliminary results are used. In case of identical margins (tied to the hundredth of a percentage point), tied options split the payout equally. Postponed elections or those without sufficient results by the deadline resolve to No.
markets.title: Will Minnesota have the smallest margin of victory in 2026 United States Senate elections?

markets.rules_primary: If NC-03 has the smallest margin of victory among all elections in the November 3, 2026 U.S. House general elections as of Jan 3, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Margin of victory is calculated as the absolute percentage point difference between first and second place finishers. For two-candidate races, this is winner's percentage minus runner-up's percentage. For multi-candidate races, only the gap between first and second counts. For ranked choice/instant runoff elections, the margin from the final round is used.

Every U.S. House general election held November 3, 2026 is compared, not only the districts listed here. Special elections to fill a vacancy do NOT count.

Votes for a candidate listed on more than one party line are combined.

If official results aren't available by the deadline but at least 95% of expected vote is counted, preliminary results are used. In case of identical margins (tied to the hundredth of a percentage point), tied options split the payout equally. Postponed elections or those without sufficient results by the deadline resolve to No.

markets.rules_primary: If the first calendar day in the 2026-27 winter season on which Big Sky Ski Resort conducts Seasonal Opening Operations occurs before Nov 15, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Seasonal Opening Operations require at least one passenger lift to carry members of the general public uphill for downhill skiing or snowboarding on terrain designated open for that use by Big Sky Ski Resort. 
The opening calendar day is determined in Eastern Time.
The season runs from September 1 through August 31 of the following year. “Before” excludes the specified date. 
A name, branding, ownership, operator, or website change does not change the resort’s geographic identity. 
If Big Sky Ski Resort is decommissioned, the market resolves to No.

Payout criteria
Access counts only when holders of a season pass valid for the specified season can use those lifts and terrain without an additional purchase.
Free reservations and passholder-only days count.
Any number of lifts, any amount of terrain, and any operating duration count.

Doesn’t count for payout
Employee, contractor, invited-media, private-event, and separately purchased early-access or preview days do not count. 
Scenic rides, mountain biking, hiking, tubing, and uphill-only access do not count.
Scheduled, projected, or announced opening dates do not count.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the Big Sky Ski Resort. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.rules_primary: If Tobey Maguire performs / is announced as Spider-Man in Avengers: Doomsday, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For the purposes of this Contract, Tobey Maguire satisfies the Payout Criterion if either:

Official Announcement:
Tobey Maguire is officially announced, confirmed, or publicly credited as cast to perform Spider-Man in Avengers: Doomsday, regardless of whether the performance ultimately occurs; OR

Actual Performance:
Tobey Maguire appears on stage, on screen, or in recorded content as Spider-Man in any official performance, showing, or release of Avengers: Doomsday.

Additional clarification(s):

If Avengers: Doomsday is entirely cancelled or abandoned before any official performance or release occurs, but Tobey Maguire was officially announced in Spider-Man, the Contract will resolve to “Yes.”

If multiple people are announced for Spider-Man (e.g., alternating cast, dual casting), and Tobey Maguire is among them, the Contract will resolve to “Yes.”

The Contract may resolve to “No” prior to the Expiration Date if:
(a) Avengers: Doomsday is cancelled or completes its run without Tobey Maguire being announced or performing in Spider-Man, or
(b) another person is officially announced as the sole exclusive performer for Spider-Man.

This market and these products have not been endorsed by Disney. Any references to Disney or any associated marks are descriptive only and do not indicate an endorsement of this product or any affiliation between Disney and Kalshi.

markets.rules_secondary:
Video Game:
For the purposes of this contract, a video game is defined as an interactive digital experience in which a user provides input that directly influences on-screen or in-environment outcomes rendered by a computer, console, or equivalent digital device.

This includes, but is not limited to:

Console games (e.g., PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo)

PC games (including downloadable or cloud-based experiences)

Mobile games (apps available on iOS, Android, or equivalent platforms)

Browser-based games playable via standard web browsers

Virtual Reality (VR) or Augmented Reality (AR) experiences that meet the interactivity requirement.

KXCRYPTOSTRUCTURE: https://kalshi.com/markets/kxcryptostructure/crypto-market-structure/kxcryptostructure-26jan

The vote must occur in the relevant full chamber (that is, not a Committee vote, though not every member of the chamber needs to have participated in the vote). If no vote has occurred before the specified date, then any market not including "zero" within its count (e.g. "Between 50 and 64") resolves to No, and any market including "zero" (e.g. "Below 50") resolves to Yes. If the vote count is not specified but the bill is passed, any market including "100" for the Senate and "435" for the House of Representatives (e.g. "Between 65 and 100" or "Between 300 and 435") will resolve to Yes, and any market not including "100" or "435", respectively, (e.g. "Below 65") resolves to No.

Once the market has expired, a request by any Member of Congress to add, remove, or alter a vote shall not be considered for purposes of resolving this market, regardless of any change to the official vote tally reported by the website Congress.gov or any other official source.

markets.rules_secondary:
This market measures threshold crossings after issuance and before January 1, 2027 at 10:00 AM EST. A single qualifying Pyth Network FX.USD/MXN aggregate price strictly greater than 19 Mexican pesos per U.S. dollar is sufficient for Yes. markets.rules_primary: If the governments of the United States and China have signed a new agreement containing a specific commitment on artificial intelligence after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify, unless the new article itself explicitly reaffirms the truth of the topic as of the publication date. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

For this market, an agreement is signed when authorized representatives of both governments sign a written agreement, treaty, memorandum of understanding, or similar instrument, or when the two governments issue a written text jointly, such as a joint statement or declaration. It must contain at least one specific commitment on artificial intelligence, meaning an action, restriction, standard, procedure, or mechanism that one or both governments agree to undertake or support. References to "superintelligence" or similar terms count as artificial intelligence.

A qualifying commitment may be part of a broader agreement, including a multilateral agreement that both governments sign. A declaration, communiqué or resolution adopted by a multilateral forum or organization, such as an APEC or G20 leaders' declaration or a UN resolution, does NOT qualify unless both governments sign it. A newly signed instrument that formalizes or implements an arrangement announced before Issuance qualifies.

The following do NOT qualify:
Separate readouts, fact sheets, press releases, or remarks by one or both governments announcing an agreement, or an agreement to sign later.
Agreements limited to future talks, general cooperation, or broad principles on AI.
Private-company or unofficial-dialogue agreements without government signature.

The signing or joint adoption must first occur after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027. An agreement signed before Issuance does NOT qualify, even if it is reported again later. The qualifying report must be originally transmitted or reported in English after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027. The original text may be in any language. Subsequent retractions or corrections of articles published after Issuance and before the deadline do not affect market resolution, and the market may resolve on original article publication.

markets.rules_primary: If the US and Canada agree to or announce a cut to or removal of US Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The tariffs refer to the additional US duties imposed under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 by Proclamations 11046, 11047 and 11048, as amended. The agreement must commit to a lower Section 338 duty, or an exemption from it, for a defined group of covered Canadian goods, including goods within an agreed quota. A change to a separate tariff or quota alone does NOT qualify.

A joint statement qualifies, as do separate official statements or notices from each government. An announcement by one government qualifies only if the other government also confirms it, and counts from the date of that confirmation. A publicly released agreement signed by both governments also qualifies. Announcements with specified future implementation dates qualify.

Unilateral tariff changes, a temporary tariff pause without an agreement, agreements that change only other tariffs, and conditional agreements where the US and Canada commit to a cut to or removal of US Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods contingent on specified circumstances do NOT qualify.

markets.rules_primary: If the United States has agreed to, signed, or accepted a new Iran-US nuclear deal before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An agreement also made with other countries (i.e. multilaterally) is still encompassed if the United States participates. "A new Iran-US nuclear deal" means a formal written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both the United States and Iran that (1) imposes verifiable restrictions on Iran's nuclear program, including limits on uranium enrichment, centrifuge numbers, or nuclear facility operations, AND (2) provides for the lifting, suspension, or modification of at least one US economic sanction on Iran in exchange for Iran's nuclear commitments.

Clarification (04/19/26): The Agreement Long rulebook variable defines the nature of the qualifying instrument: it must be a formal written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both governments. It does not impose a precondition that the signing itself must occur before resolution. Because the Payout Criterion is satisfied if the United States has "agreed to, signed, or accepted" such an instrument, both governments publicly and officially agreeing to the terms of what will be a qualifying written agreement is sufficient to resolve the market to Yes, even if the formal signing has not yet taken place.

Clarification (06/02/26): A qualifying instrument must impose "verifiable restrictions on Iran's nuclear program." A restriction is "verifiable" only where it establishes a concrete, objectively ascertainable standard (a defined limit, prohibition, quantity, or monitoring provision) against which compliance could in principle be confirmed; a general expression of intent that fixes no such standard is not considered “verifiable” for the purposes of this event. Accordingly, a bare pledge not to develop or pursue nuclear weapons, unaccompanied by any concrete limit on Iran's nuclear materials, activities, or facilities, does not on its own satisfy criterion (1). Conversely, a commitment to completely 'stop' or ‘suspend’ a specific nuclear activity (such as uranium enrichment) establishes a concrete prohibition (an implicit limit of zero) and qualifies as a restriction, whereas a vague promise to 'reduce' activities without a defined metric or monitoring mechanism does not. The enumerated examples (limits on uranium enrichment, centrifuge numbers, or nuclear facility operations) are illustrative and not exhaustive: a formal, verifiable commitment to remove, transfer, or cap Iran's stock of enriched uranium, confirmable by the receiving state or an oversight body, is a restriction on Iran's nuclear program and satisfies criterion (1). In every case, criterion (2) must independently be met.

Clarification (06/17/26): To clarify, the U.S.–Iran memorandum of understanding reportedly now in effect does not satisfy criterion (1) of the definition of a "new Iran-US nuclear deal," and this market will therefore not resolve to Yes on the basis of that instrument at this time. The memorandum provides for the existing state of Iran's nuclear program to be maintained pending a subsequent agreement, and defers the disposition of Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium to a mechanism to be mutually agreed in that subsequent agreement. That it states a minimum methodology for that future mechanism — down-blending on site under IAEA supervision — constrains the form of a mechanism yet to be agreed, but specifies no quantity, enrichment level, or completion deadline for the down-blending. An instrument that provides for maintaining Iran's nuclear program at an unspecified status quo, or that defers its substantive nuclear commitments to a subsequent agreement, does not by itself establish the concrete, objectively ascertainable standard that a "verifiable" restriction requires.

markets.rules_primary: If the value of S&P/TSX Composite Index (TSX) is at least 36,000 from Jul 9, 2026 to Dec 31, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market resolves based on the value of the S&P/TSX Composite Index as reported by the Trading View, using the index's natively published level in its own currency and units; no currency conversion is applied. It is sufficient for the index to reach or exceed 36,000 at any single point from Jul 9, 2026 to Dec 31, 2026 for the market to resolve to Yes — the level does not need to be sustained. If no data is available from Jul 9, 2026 to Dec 31, 2026 by the Expiration Date, all strikes other than "No data" or "None" resolve to No. The index level is evaluated to two decimal places unless otherwise specified.

markets.rules_primary: If any federal or state court issues a preliminary or permanent injunction prohibiting Trump Media & Technology Group from providing paying customers faster access to Donald Trump's Truth Social posts than is available to the general public in a case concerning paid early access to Donald Trump's Truth Social posts before Dec 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The ruling must:
Be issued by any federal or state court in a case concerning paid early access to Donald Trump's Truth Social posts
Address the matter described by the specified judgment
Be issued through a written order, opinion, judgment, or decision

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Oral rulings from the bench unless reduced to a written order
Tentative rulings that are not made final
Draft opinions that leak but are not officially issued
Settlements or voluntary dismissals
Administrative or scheduling orders
Orders to show cause
Minute orders that do not address the substantive issue in the specified judgment

markets.rules_secondary:
The following do NOT constitute a visit:

Flying over the area without landing
Layovers during which the person remains in an airplane
Virtual or remote appearances
Presence in international waters adjacent to the area
Presence solely within embassy or consulate grounds
Plans, announcements, or scheduling of future visits that do not occur during the applicable time period

For the avoidance of doubt, a visit occurs only when the person exits an aircraft, vehicle, vessel, or train within the area, or otherwise physically enters the area not aboard one. Remaining aboard, including during flyovers, drive-throughs, and non-exit refueling stops, does not constitute a visit. Exiting within the area constitutes a visit regardless of duration or method of exit.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the visit occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If Donald Trump has physically travelled to and been present within the geographic boundaries of Israel after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The following do NOT constitute a visit:

Flying over the area without landing
Layovers during which the person remains in an airplane
Virtual or remote appearances
Presence in international waters adjacent to the area
Presence solely within embassy or consulate grounds
Plans, announcements, or scheduling of future visits that do not occur during the applicable time period

For the avoidance of doubt, a visit occurs only when the person exits an aircraft, vehicle, vessel, or train within the area, or otherwise physically enters the area not aboard one. Remaining aboard, including during flyovers, drive-throughs, and non-exit refueling stops, does not constitute a visit. Exiting within the area constitutes a visit regardless of duration or method of exit.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If Donald Trump sits for a deposition in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This must be confirmed, verified, or established as factual by at least one Source Agency.

News confirmation is defined as a published article, broadcast segment, or official news report by a Source Agency, that A) explicitly states Donald Trump sitting for a deposition in his defamation lawsuit against the BBC occurred, is true, or has been verified, B) based on journalistic investigation, sources, or evidence, and C) presented as factual reporting rather than speculation, rumor, or unverified allegation.

Sitting for a deposition means Donald Trump personally appeared and gave sworn oral testimony, in person or by remote video, at a deposition taken in the defamation action he filed against the British Broadcasting Corporation in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida. A deposition that begins and is then adjourned, suspended, or continued qualifies once he has been sworn and has answered questions.

The following do NOT count:
A deposition that is noticed, scheduled, agreed to, or ordered by the court but not actually held
Affidavits, declarations, sworn written statements, or answers to written interrogatories
Testimony at a hearing, at trial, or before Congress
A deposition taken in any other case or proceeding
A deposition of any person other than Donald Trump

markets.rules_primary: If Taylor Swift is Time Person of the Year for 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This will count towards the payout criterion: 
If multiple persons win, all persons that are listed are encompassed within the Payout Criterion. If, for example, the Person of the Year is “Joe Biden and Kamala Harris”, both “Joe Biden” and “Kamala Harris” strikes are encompassed within the Payout Criterion. 
The person must be explicitly named as the Person of the Year or pictured on the/a relevant cover if they are associated with the group/concept winning (the picture is only relevant for a natural human being winning). Some examples to illustrate this: “Jamal Khasogghi” would resolve to Yes in 2018, when “The Guardians” won, as he is also named and shown on a cover and falls within “The Guardians”. Similarly, “Bill Gates” would resolve to Yes in 2005. 
If Time uses language that does not specifically refer to a person or organization (examples being 2018’s “The Guardians” or 2017’s “The Silence Breakers”), Kalshi will resolve markets to the most simple meaning reasonable. In those cases, “Journalists” and “the Me Too movement” would resolve to Yes.

This does NOT count towards the payout criterion: 
If there is no Person of the Year (and instead many variations thereof, e.g. Entertainer of the Year, Hero of the Year), that is not encompassed in the Payout Criterion. 
If “ChatGPT” was the Person of the Year, strikes of “AI” or “LLMs” would resolve to No, since even if they are conceptually linked, they are not synonymous (and thus are not explicitly named), and are not persons, so it would not matter if they were identified in the image. Or if “Sam Altman” was the Person of the Year, and the cover showed a person using ChatGPT on their computer, “ChatGPT” would not resolve to Yes because it is not a person.

This market and these products have not been endorsed by TIME. Any references to TIME, or any associated marks are descriptive only and do not indicate an endorsement of this product or any affiliation between TIME and Kalshi.
